sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed (construct used for surface-display experiments); electrophysiological function NOT MEASURED in the cited clip.
sites.rationale: N134 falls within EC1 (topology landmarks: extracellular 81–171), 54 residues from the TM1 C-boundary (residue 80) and 38 residues from the TM2 N-boundary (residue 172), satisfying the ≥3-residue clearance rule with wide margin. Python confirmed seq[133]='N' and seq[134]='T', matching the paper's stated junction exactly. The paper explicitly describes this as a surface-display construct, providing direct evidence of extracellular accessibility. No residue-level ambiguity exists; the paper names N134 unambiguously. Full-length TREK-1 (KCNK2) with HA tag (YPYDVPDYA) inserted immediately after residue N134 in the extracellular loop connecting the cap and P1 helix; construct expressed in mammalian cells for surface-display experiments; sequence-verified by Sanger sequencing.

sources.claim: TREK1 HA was generated by inserting an HA tag (YPYDVPDYA) immediately following residue N134 in the loop connecting the cap and P1 helix using the Q5 mutagenesis kit (New England Biosciences) following the manufacturer’s protocol for large insertions using non-overlapping primers and was sequence-verified (Genewiz).

literature_notes: L2 (PMC3411076) reports an N-terminal HA tag on a concatenated TREK-1 construct. The KCNK2 N-terminus (residue 1) is intracellular per topology landmarks (IC: 1–61); this tag faces the cytoplasm and does not qualify as a surface tag site. L3 (PMC10592817) reports a C-terminal EGFP fusion used for dSTORM imaging; the C-terminus (residue 426) is intracellular per topology landmarks (IC: 309–426) and likewise does not qualify. Both are recorded in other_positions. No ledger evidence supports a tag in EC2 (246–287) or at any other extracellular position.
